# `select_time_grid`

the dyadic time grid of a recording's line, one rule family (tiles, band, frames, constant-Q, segments, windows, chunks), with the frame density and the origin as options.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run select_time_grid --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run select_time_grid --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run select_time_grid --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --rule frames --band "8-12 Hz"
nxr-neuro run select_time_grid --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --rule constant_q --range "0.5-64 Hz"
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, each true, where {"name": "$recording"} | yes |
| `line` | manifold line, is recording.time | yes |
| `event` | selection any, manifold recording.time, where {"name": "$origin_event"}, required false (an origin given as an event: the stored selection whose first member starts the grid) | no |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | `--recording` | `none` | - |  | the recording's name, or none: every recording of the subject, one run each |
| `rule` | `--rule` | `tiles` | - | tiles, band, frames, constant_q, segments, windows, chunks | how the width is resolved: tiles \| band \| frames \| constant_q \| segments \| windows \| chunks |
| `duration` | `--duration` | none | s |  | rules tiles, segments, windows: the tile, segment or window as a duration |
| `band` | `--band` | none | Hz |  | rules band and frames: the band in Hz, e.g. "8-12 Hz" (a list for rule constant_q's bands is `range`) |
| `range` | `--range` | `0.5-64 Hz` | Hz |  | rule constant_q: the ladder's frequency range |
| `voices` | `--voices` | `1` | voices/octave |  | rule constant_q: bands per octave |
| `cycles` | `--cycles` | `4` | cycles |  | rules band and frames: cycles of the band's centre one tile holds (the Studio's fitLevelOf) |
| `frames_per_cycle` | `--frames-per-cycle` | `36` | frames/cycle |  | rule frames: frames to one cycle of the band's centre (the 10 degree step of phase work); the alternative to frames_per_tile |
| `frames_per_tile` | `--frames-per-tile` | none | frames/tile |  | rule frames: frames to one tile of the band (a power of two); when given it wins over frames_per_cycle |
| `overlap` | `--overlap` | `0.5` | fraction |  | rule segments: the fraction of a segment shared with the next |
| `step` | `--step` | none | s |  | rule windows: the step between windows; null: the window (no overlap) |
| `origin` | `--origin` | `start` | - | start, clock, event | the grid's origin as a point: start (the recording's first sample) \| clock (seconds from local midnight, given in origin_clock) \| event (the stored selection named by origin_event) |
| `origin_clock` | `--origin-clock` | none | s |  | origin clock: the time of day of the recording's first sample, as 'HH:MM:SS' or seconds |
| `origin_event` | `--origin-event` | none | - |  | origin event: the name of the stored selection whose first member is the origin |
| `name` | `--name` | `{recording} time grid {grid_rule}` | - |  | the grid's row, NAMED BY ITS RULE (`{grid_rule}`: band 8-16 Hz, frames 8-12 Hz 36 per cycle, constant_q 0.5-64 Hz 1 voices, tiles 1 s, ...): several grids coexist on a line and a consumer finds its own by that name |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`select.time_grid`](../nodes.md) | line=line, event=event | rule=$rule, duration=$duration, band=$band, range=$range, voices=$voices, cycles=$cycles, frames_per_cycle=$frames_per_cycle, frames_per_tile=$frames_per_tile, overlap=$overlap, step=$step, origin=$origin | grid |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `grid` | kind selection, type tiling, on recording.time, name $name |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE TIME GRID OF A LINE: ONE maker (the node `select.time_grid`), one rule family: every member is [origin + i hop, origin + i hop + width) on the line's samples, width and hop 2^k samples (the Studio's `timeTiling`,
nxr `time_grid`). The rules differ only in how the width is resolved from the stated QUANTITY (never a level index):

  tiles        a duration (s): the first 2^k samples at least it (`natural_level`)
  band         a band (Hz): the first 2^k holding `cycles` cycles of its centre sqrt(lo hi) (the Studio's `fitLevelOf`, 4 cycles)
  frames       a band and a FRAME DENSITY: frames per cycle of the band's centre (default 36, the phase work's 10 degree step) OR frames per tile; the frame is the dyadic tile nearest the density asks for
  constant_q   a frequency range and voices per octave: one level per band of the ladder, each carrying the Studio's ConstantQLevelInfo (low_hz, high_hz, centre, window, ...)
  segments     a duration and an overlap (Welch's segments: members overlap, a family not a partition)
  windows      a window duration and a step
  chunks       none: the chunk grid (2^15 samples)

THE ORIGIN of a grid is a POINT, an option of the run: the recording's start (`start`, the default), a clock time (`clock 14:30:00`, seconds from local midnight) or an EVENT (a stored selection's
first member: `event <name>`). Frame density and origin are options with their defaults WRITTEN HERE; no method constant is hard-wired in compute.

What it cannot resolve: a frame is a dyadic tile, so the stated density is met to within the nearest power of two (the snapped frame length is recorded in provenance as seconds and as frames per cycle).

  nxr-neuro run select_time_grid --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --rule frames --band "8-12 Hz"
  nxr-neuro run select_time_grid --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --rule constant_q --range "0.5-64 Hz"
```
